condition: calcium-channel-blocker associated bilateral afternoon pitting ankle swelling leaving thumb indentations for 2 weeks after starting daily amlodipine
level_rationale: Two weeks of daily afternoon swelling in both ankles that leaves a thumb dent when pressed starting shortly after initiating daily amlodipine 3 weeks ago in a 56-year-old adult describes classic dihydropyridine calcium-channel-blocker peripheral pitting edema warranting a routine outpatient physician visit to confirm benign drug-induced vasodilatory edema and adjust antihypertensive therapy rather than unguided self-care or emergency care, whereas noticing slight puffiness around both ankles for 10 minutes on 1 afternoon last week after starting daily amlodipine represents a trivial transient observation needing only routine home self-care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + Rule A first-choice ankle swelling severity and duration de-escalation control (-cf, L2 to L1), written without apostrophe contractions.

design_note: Three atomic reference facts cover age 56, starting daily amlodipine 3 weeks ago, and 2 weeks of bilateral afternoon ankle swelling leaving a thumb dent when pressed, with an exact 0-word span difference (18 vs 18 words) and zero contractions. Under Rule A first choice and Rule D, reducing f3 at the exact same bilateral ankles to 10 minutes of slight puffiness on 1 afternoon last week preserves coherent medication-monitoring context while shifting care cleanly from doctor review (level 2) to routine self-care (level 1).
